slice_results.behavior_summary: When called, the code registers a video.js caption plugin that manages caption display by reading caption data passed in options and updating DOM overlays accordingly. It accesses and modifies caption text and styles, processes custom tags in captions, and handles playback time updates to synchronize captions. No network, file, system, or cryptographic APIs are accessed or executed, and no suspicious hardcoded IPs, URLs, commands, or encoded strings are present, resulting in no security-sensitive operations.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code is a video.js caption plugin that manages caption display and styling based on playback time. It processes caption data, updates DOM overlays, and handles user interactions related to captions. There are no network calls, no dynamic script injections, no obfuscation, no access to sensitive system or cryptographic APIs, and no evidence of data exfiltration or command execution. The code does not match the known malicious patterns, which involve injection of arbitrary HTML leading to XSS, script injection from untrusted sources, or trojanized libraries. The plugin operates purely on local caption data and DOM manipulation in a legitimate manner.

matched_snippet.code_snippet: <figcaption class="cke_widget_editable" data-placeholder="Enter caption here" data-cke-widget-editable="caption" data-cke-enter-mode="2" data-cke-filter="46" data-cke-display-name="caption" contenteditable="true">I am a caption</figcaption>
matched_snippet.code_behavior: During content creation or editing, the code allows arbitrary HTML and attributes to be inserted into the figcaption element, which is then stored in the Drupal database and rendered in the page body, resulting in the injection of malicious content or attributes into the DOM.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The snippet permits arbitrary HTML and attributes in a context that is rendered as part of the page, allowing attackers to inject malicious code or attributes that can alter page behavior or facilitate XSS.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict HTML and attributes in figcaption to a safe, predefined whitelist; here, arbitrary attributes and classes are allowed, breaking containment and enabling injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to style captions or add semantic markup, but not to allow arbitrary classes or data attributes that could be abused for XSS or UI manipulation.
key_indicators: Lack of attribute sanitization in figcaption
Ability to inject arbitrary classes and data-* attributes
Presence of non-whitelisted attributes in rendered HTML

package_info.why_malicious: Multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into user-generated content. These flaws bypass expected sanitization, enabling stored and self-XSS, page defacement, and user redirection. The vulnerabilities break HTML sandboxing and can be exploited by low-privileged users to execute malicious scripts in the context of other users.

attack_chain.leads_to: XSS, page defacement, or user redirection occurs as the malicious content is executed in the victim's browser.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-generated content in the Drupal database and rendered pages for <script> tags, javascript: URLs in HTML attributes, and suspicious classes or data-* attributes in figcaption and widget HTML. Monitor for DOM elements with overlay classes or non-whitelisted attributes. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block known XSS payloads and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity originating from user interaction with content, such as redirections or JavaScript-initiated requests to external domains.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: During user input in source mode, the code injects a <script> tag into the data-caption attribute, which is rendered in preview mode, resulting in the execution of arbitrary JavaScript and triggering a browser alert.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The injection of <script> tags into user-editable fields without proper sanitization enables execution of arbitrary JavaScript, which is a critical XSS vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior should sanitize or escape script tags in captions to prevent script execution. Here, the preview mode fails to sanitize input, allowing direct execution of user-supplied scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use case for allowing script tags in image captions; captions should only contain safe, sanitized text or basic formatting.

package_info.why_malicious: Drupal Core contains multiple cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling logic. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes into content, leading to account hijacking, web content injection, page defacement, and redirection attacks. The root cause is inconsistent sanitization between client-side and server-side code, and insufficient attribute whitelisting, which enables malicious payloads to bypass security controls.

matched_knowledge.source_package: Trojanized jQuery (multiple packages, e.g., icnes, stylesyosx, imagegs, etc.) (npm (also distributed via GitHub and jsDelivr CDN))

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, when the script is loaded, the code injects external scripts into the page, including a deprecated version of Ionicons and a remote script (slim.js) hosted on jsDelivr, which itself contains the trojanized jQuery. This enables the delivery and execution of further malicious payloads and establishes persistence for the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting remote scripts from untrusted or attacker-controlled sources is a common technique for loading additional malware. The use of misleading deprecation warnings and outdated libraries is intended to trick users or developers into trusting the injected content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal icon libraries do not inject unrelated remote scripts or force the use of outdated versions without user consent. They also do not load scripts from untrusted CDNs or chain to further malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection is sometimes used by legitimate plugin loaders, but not in core icon libraries and never with misleading warnings or by loading unrelated, potentially malicious scripts.
key_indicators: Dynamic injection of remote scripts from attacker-controlled or untrusted CDNs
Use of misleading deprecation warnings to mask malicious activity
Loading of outdated or unrelated library versions
Chaining to further malicious payloads (e.g., slim.js containing trojanized jQuery)
Script injection occurring outside of user-initiated actions

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when icons.js or min.js is loaded and executed in the browser (typically during page load or dynamic script injection).
execution_context.file_location: icons.js, min.js (in package root or distributed via CDN)

package_info.package_name: Trojanized jQuery (multiple packages, e.g., icnes, stylesyosx, imagegs, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (also distributed via GitHub and jsDelivr CDN)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple (see list, e.g., icnes@8.0.0, stylesyosx@9.0.3, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain a trojanized version of jQuery in which the 'end' prototype function is maliciously modified to exfiltrate all form data from the page to attacker-controlled domains whenever it is called, either directly or indirectly (such as via fadeTo). The packages are distributed under misleading names, often include personal files unrelated to the package's purpose, and use unique exfiltration URLs to evade detection. This enables large-scale theft of sensitive user input (credentials, PII, etc.) from any site using the compromised packages.

attack_chain.action: User installs or includes a malicious package (via npm, GitHub, or CDN).
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojanized jQuery or loader script is present in the application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious jQuery file (or loader script) is loaded and executed in the browser, often via dynamic script injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojanized jQuery is present in the page context, ready to intercept user actions.

attack_chain.action: User or application code calls jQuery's end or fadeTo function (directly or indirectly), triggering the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious end function is executed, capturing form data.

attack_chain.action: All form data on the page is serialized, hex-encoded, and exfiltrated via a GET request to an attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user input (credentials, PII, etc.) from the compromised site.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for unauthorized modifications to core library prototype methods, especially jQuery's end. Use static analysis to compare jQuery source code against known-good versions and flag any added network or data exfiltration logic. Monitor for unexpected network requests containing serialized or hex-encoded form data sent to suspicious or attacker-controlled domains. Flag packages that include personal files or inject remote scripts from untrusted sources. Analyze icon and utility scripts for dynamic script injection and misleading deprecation warnings. Combine static and dynamic analysis to detect both code modifications and runtime exfiltration behaviors.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, on page load or script execution, the code injects external scripts into the page, including a deprecated version of Ionicons and a remote script (slim.js) hosted on jsDelivr, which itself contains the trojanized jQuery. This enables further malicious code execution and persistence by loading additional payloads from attacker-controlled sources.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script injects remote code from attacker-controlled sources without user consent, using a misleading deprecation warning to disguise its activity and facilitate further compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not inject remote scripts or downgrade libraries without explicit user action or clear documentation. Core libraries should not dynamically load external code from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection is used in some legitimate plugin loaders, but not in core libraries or without user awareness and explicit opt-in.

Flag any code that serializes and exfiltrates form data to external domains. matched_knowledge.source_package: Boom! Mobile website (boom[.]us) Magecart skimmer (N/A (injected JavaScript on e-commerce website))

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At page load, the code loads an external JavaScript skimmer from a Base64-encoded URL, executes it in the context of the checkout page, and enables the interception of payment form data for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Loading an external script from a Base64-encoded URL is a deliberate obfuscation technique to evade static detection and code review. The script source is not associated with the legitimate business and points to a suspicious, attacker-controlled domain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce sites should only load scripts from trusted, first-party, or well-known third-party sources. The use of Base64-encoded script sources and unrecognized domains is not expected in production environments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Base64-encoded script URLs are almost never used in legitimate production e-commerce environments, as they complicate maintenance and security reviews.
key_indicators: Base64-encoded external script source in <script> tag
Script loaded from a domain not associated with the business (e.g., google-standard[.]com)
Script injection on sensitive payment or checkout pages

execution_context.trigger: At page load (when user accesses the payment/checkout page)
execution_context.file_location: Injected inline in HTML or as an external script reference (e.g., <script> tag on payment page)

package_info.why_malicious: The website was compromised by attackers who injected a malicious JavaScript skimmer. This script intercepts and exfiltrates payment card and private data entered by customers during checkout to attacker-controlled domains, constituting a classic Magecart attack targeting e-commerce transactions.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to the website and injects a malicious script tag with a Base64-encoded external source into the payment or checkout page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious skimmer script is loaded and executed in the context of the checkout page.

attack_chain.action: The external skimmer script executes, hooks into the payment form's submit event, and collects user-entered payment and personal data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Collected payment and personal data is prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The skimmer script sends the stolen payment and personal data to attacker-controlled domains via HTTPS POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credit card and personal information from compromised customers.

behavioral_signatures: Inline or external scripts loaded from non-standard, suspicious, or recently registered domains on payment or checkout pages
Base64-encoded script sources in HTML <script> tags
JavaScript code that hooks form submission events and sends collected data to external domains
file_indicators: References to domains such as google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, google-money[.]com in script sources
Unexpected or unauthorized script tags present on payment or checkout pages
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains like google-standard[.]com, bing-analytics[.]com, google-money[.]com during checkout or payment form submission
Unusual network traffic to recently registered or non-canonical domains originating from payment pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for <script> tags in HTML that load resources from suspicious or encoded sources, especially on payment or checkout pages. Inspect JavaScript for event listeners on forms that collect and send data to external domains. Use network monitoring to detect POST requests to known skimmer domains. Flag any new or unrecognized domains in script sources or network traffic, particularly those registered recently or not associated with the business. Correlate script injection events with anomalous network activity to identify active skimming.
